parts.content:
The claim is directly confirmed. `student.sessionToken` is a credential field (types.ts:4), and it is written to the console at instrumentation-client.ts:19 inside `recordSessionStart`. That is exactly the offending token-logging statement the rule targets.

There is a second violation at renamed-and-edited.ts:12, but the claim points at the instrumentation-client.ts:19 statement, which is real.

arguments.rationale: Confirmed violation. In /qa2671/instrumentation-client.ts:19, `recordSessionStart` executes `console.log('session start', student.id, student.sessionToken)`, writing the session token to application logs/telemetry. The Student type (/qa2671/types.ts:4) declares `sessionToken: string` as a credential field. The claim's citation of file:line matches the actual offending statement. (A second, similar leak exists at /qa2671/renamed-and-edited.ts:12, `console.info('student auth', student.sessionToken)`, reinforcing the pattern.) The rule prohibits session tokens in logs; the code does not remove or redact the token, so the claim stands.
